title: Add RAG Replay Lab and Tool-call Fuzzer Quickstart
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Adds an interactive RAG Replay Lab quickstart with a tool-call fuzzer harness, devcontainer, session recorder/playback, and lightweight e2e smoke tests.
description: Motivation: engineers frequently need a compact, reproducible environment to iterate on tool-calling behavior and regression test retrieval-augmented agents under synthetic but realistic user flows. This quickstart introduces a Replay Lab that records simulated sessions (prompt sequence + tool calls + tool responses) and a complementary tool-call fuzzer that injects network and tool-level edge conditions to surface robustness regressions. The goal is to give engineers a local-first loop for: 1) capturing a failing session from production or CI, 2) replaying it against new model/config variants, 3) running a deterministic fuzzer to exercise tool bindings and structured-output contracts, and 4) asserting invariants via lightweight contract tests and telemetry probes. What this PR adds: - quickstarts/replay-lab/README.md: walkthrough and concepts for recording, replaying, and writing assertions. - quickstarts/replay-lab/devcontainer/: VSCode devcontainer + docker-compose for local runners. - quickstarts/replay-lab/recorder: small Go-based session recorder that captures request/response envelopes and kv-cache warmup traces. - quickstarts/replay-lab/player: Node-based deterministic player that can run sessions in headless mode and emit structured-output diffs. - quickstarts/replay-lab/fuzzer: Python harness that mutates tool responses, simulates latencies, and toggles transient errors for tool-call paths. - quickstarts/replay-lab/tests/: playwright smoke e2e + contract assertions that run in CI. - quickstarts/replay-lab/example-corpus/: three curated example sessions (search-and-lookup, multi-tool itinerary, and invoice extraction) used by tests and demos. - CI workflow quickstarts/replay-lab/ci.yml: smoke runner job and matrix config for node/python versions. Developer checklist (included in README): - [x] Capture session via recorder - [x] Replay locally using player - [x] Run fuzzer against tool stubs - [x] Add contract assertions for structured output - [x] Run CI smoke job The description contains a short troubleshooting section and tips for pairing with Redwood Console telemetry (how to correlate session ids). Backwards compatibility: all added code is opt-in under the quickstarts path and does not change any platform API. The recorder/player work over the standard Redwood API surface and default auth; no changes to core runtime. Testing: local devcontainer smoke run + CI matrix. Performance: n/a for production runtime. Rollout: documents and quickstart merged to main and published to docs site via the docs pipeline. Related work: builds on ENG-1423 (replayability RFC) and ENG-1588 (tool-call contract spec).

review_comments: Evan Cho: Nice end-to-end. Can we make the session envelope schema stable (versioned) so future players can ignore unknown fields?
Priya Patel: Good call. Bumped envelope to v1 and added a version field in recorder output. Updated README and tests to assert version.
Liam O'Connor: Fuzzer looks useful. Please add a timeout so a runaway mutation loop doesn't stall CI.
Priya Patel: Added --max-iterations and CI ensures a bounded run. Also added a CI-only flag to disable heavy fuzz runs on PRs.
Maya Singh: Playwright job flaked once on linux-node; please pin node versions in matrix and retry the job.
CI Bot: replay-lab smokes (linux, node14/node16) rerun passed on second attempt and was green.
Liam O'Connor: Approved after minor CI tweaks. Evan Approved. Merged by Priya via squash.
